b2-panama-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The Jungle Without a Road
b2-panama-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about the Darién, and he asks what you learned about the Pan-American Highway.
b2-panama-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what happens to the highway in the Darién.
cues: Say that the highway runs along almost the whole continent
Say that it stops in the Darién
b2-panama-01.target: La Carretera Panamericana, que recorre casi todo el continente, se interrumpe en el Darién.
b2-panama-01.english: The Pan-American Highway, which runs along almost the whole continent, stops in the Darién.
b2-panama-01.canDo: I can describe the isthmus and the Darién with relative clauses (*que*, *quien*).

b2-panama-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Before the Canal
b2-panama-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading an article about the Panama Canal, and she asks you how ships travelled before it existed.
b2-panama-02.prompt: Tell Meg what ships had to do before the canal existed.
cues: Say what ships had to do
Say that this was before the canal existed
b2-panama-02.target: Antes de que existiera el canal, los barcos tenían que rodear América del Sur.
b2-panama-02.english: Before the canal existed, ships had to sail round South America.
b2-panama-02.canDo: I can say what happened before or after an event in the history of the canal, with *antes de que* and *después de que*.

b2-panama-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Essential but Paid Less
b2-panama-03.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are listening to a talk about the Afro-Antillean workers of the canal, and he asks you what struck you most.
b2-panama-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what you noticed about the workers on the silver list.
cues: Say that their work was essential
Say that they were paid less
b2-panama-03.target: Si bien su trabajo era esencial, los trabajadores de la lista de plata cobraban menos.
b2-panama-03.english: Although their work was essential, the workers on the silver list were paid less.
b2-panama-03.canDo: I can grant a point in a formal sentence with *si bien* and the indicative.

b2-panama-04.title: Communicative Challenge: What Is Sold in Colón
b2-panama-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading an article about Panama's economy, and she asks what the Colón Free Zone is for.
b2-panama-04.prompt: Tell Meg what happens to goods in the Colón Free Zone.
cues: Say that goods are sold there
Say that they are later re-exported
b2-panama-04.target: En la Zona Libre de Colón se venden mercancías que luego se reexportan a otros países.
b2-panama-04.english: In the Colón Free Zone goods are sold which are later re-exported to other countries.
b2-panama-04.canDo: I can say what is sold, used or published in Panama with the *se* passive.

b2-panama-05.title: Communicative Challenge: However Much the Sea Rises
b2-panama-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a report about Gardi Sugdub, and he asks what the scientists say about the sea.
b2-panama-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what will happen to the sea level, whatever happens to emissions.
cues: Say that the sea level will keep rising
b2-panama-05.target: Por más que bajen las emisiones, el nivel del mar seguirá subiendo.
b2-panama-05.english: However much emissions fall, the sea level will keep rising.
b2-panama-05.canDo: I can say that nothing changes however much something happens, with *por más que* and *por mucho que*.

b2-panama-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Panama in Review
b2-panama-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are preparing a short talk about Panama, and you want to give her one example of what you will say about the canal.
b2-panama-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg what the canal does and who has had it since 1999.
cues: Say that the canal joins two oceans
Say that it has been in Panama's hands since 1999
b2-panama-consolidation.target: El canal, que une dos océanos, está en manos de Panamá desde 1999.
b2-panama-consolidation.english: The canal, which joins two oceans, has been in Panama's hands since 1999.
b2-panama-consolidation.canDo: I can describe a place or a person with *que* and *quien*.
